At $T(K), K_c$ for the reaction
$\mathrm{AO}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{BO}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{AO}_3(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{BO}(\mathrm{g})$ is 16 . One mole each of reactants and products are taken in a 1 L flask and heated to $T(K)$, and equilibrium is established. What is the equilibrium concentration of BO (in $\mathrm{mol} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$ )?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{AO}_3\right][\mathrm{BO}]}{\left[\mathrm{AO}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{BO}_2\right]}=16$ Initial concentrations :- $\left[\mathrm{AO}_3\right]=[\mathrm{BO}]=\left[\mathrm{AO}_2\right]=\left[\mathrm{BO}_2\right]=\frac{1.0 \mathrm{~mol}}{1.0 \mathrm{~L}}=10 \mathrm{M}$ \begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|}\hline Conc. & {\left[\mathrm{AO}_2\right]} & {\left[\mathrm{BO}_2\right]} & {\left[\mathrm{AO}_3\right]} & {[\mathrm{BO}]} \\\hline Initial & 1.0 & 1.0 & 1.0 & 1.0 \\\hline At equilibrium & 1-\alpha & 1-\alpha & 1+\alpha & 1+\alpha \\\hline\end{array}
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{(1+\alpha) \times(1+\alpha)}{(1-\alpha)(1-\alpha)}=16 \\ & \frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}=4 \\ & \therefore \quad 1+\alpha=4-4 \alpha \\ & 5 \alpha=3 \\ & \alpha=3 / 5=0.6 \end{aligned}\therefore$ Equilibrium concentration of $[\mathrm{BO}]$ is $=1+0.6=1.6$.

$\begin{aligned} & \ln \frac{x}{m}=\ln k+\frac{1}{n} \ln p \\ & \text { or, } \log \frac{x}{m}=\log k+\frac{1}{n} \log p \\ & y=c+m x \\ & \text { Slope }(m)=\frac{1}{n} \quad \therefore \quad \frac{1}{n}=0.5 \\ & \text { Intercept }(\mathrm{c})=\log k=1 \\ & \text { Pressure }(p)=100 \text { atm } \\ & \therefore \log \frac{x}{m}=1+0.5 \log 10^2 \\ & \log \frac{x}{m}=1+0.5 \times 2 \Rightarrow \log \frac{x}{m}=2 \\ & \frac{x}{m}=10^2=100\end{aligned}$

Equation of tangent at vertex $=\frac{y-\frac{7}{2}}{x-\frac{3}{2}}=1\Rightarrow y=x+2$.

questions.solution:
Sum of numbers can be $2,3,5,7,11$. Multiples of 3 are 3 and 6. Sum of numbers such that 3 or 6 appears on top among the pair of numbers can be $5,7,11$. $\begin{aligned} & 5 \rightarrow(2,3)(3,2) \\ & 7 \rightarrow(4,3)(3,4)(6,1)(1,6) \\ & 11 \rightarrow(5,6)(6,5) \end{aligned}$
No. of cases $=8$ Sum can be prime in following cases : $\begin{aligned} & (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,2),(4,3),(3,4),(6,1), \\ & (1,6),(5,6),(6,5),(4,1),(1,4),(5,2),(2,5) \\ & \text { No. of cases }=15 \\ & \text { Required probability }=\frac{8}{15} .\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
We know that condition of exactly one common root of quadratic equations $a_1 x^2+b_1 x+c_1=0$ and $a_2 x^2+b_2 x+c_2=0$ is $\left(c_1 a_2-c_2 a_1\right)^2=\left(b_1 c_2-b_2 c_1\right)\left(a_1 b_2-a_2 b_1\right)$
Here, $a_1=2, b_1=a, c_1=-2, a_2=1, b_2=1$ and $c_2=2 a\begin{aligned} & \therefore(-2-4 a)^2=\left(2 a^2+2\right)(2-a) \\ & \Rightarrow 16 a^2+4+16 a=4 a^2-2 a^3+4-2 a \\ & \Rightarrow 2 a^3+12 a^2+18 a=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 a\left(a^2+6 a+9\right)=0 \Rightarrow 2 a(a+3)^2=0 \\ & \therefore a=-3 \quad(\because a \neq 0) \end{aligned}\therefore$ Given equation is $\begin{aligned} & -3 x^2-4 x+6=0 \Rightarrow 3 x^2+4 x-6=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{88}}{6}=\frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{22}}{3} \therefore x=\frac{-2+\sqrt{22}}{3} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two positive point charges are separated by a distance of 4 m in air. If the sum of the two charges is $36 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and the electrostatic force between them is 0.18 N , then the bigger charge is
questions.solution:
Electrostatic force $\mathrm{F}=\frac{\mathrm{K}_1 \mathrm{Q}_2}{\mathrm{r}^2}\begin{aligned} & \mathbf{F}=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times(\mathrm{Q}) \times\left(36 \times 10^{-6}-\mathrm{Q}\right)}{(4)^2} \\ & \text { or, } \quad 0.18=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times \mathrm{Q} \times\left(36 \times 10^{-6}-\mathrm{Q}\right)}{16}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{18 \times 10^{-2} \times 16}{9 \times 10^9}=\mathrm{Q} \times\left(36 \times 10^{-6}-\mathrm{Q}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 32 \times 10^{-11}=\mathrm{Q} \times\left(36 \times 10^{-6}-\mathrm{Q}\right) \end{aligned}$
Solving we get $\mathrm{Q}=20 \times 10^{-6}=20 \mu \mathrm{c}$ and $36 \times 10^{-6}-20 \times 10^{-6}=16 \times 10^{-6}=16 \mu \mathrm{c}$ Therefore the bigger charge is $20 \mu \mathrm{c}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy required to take a body from the surface of the earth to a height equal to the radius of the earth is ' $W$ '. The energy required to take this body from the surface of the earth to a height equal to twice the radius of the earth is
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity $g$ varies with height as $g^{\prime}=g\left(\frac{R}{R+h}\right)$
Acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to the radius of the earth $g^{\prime}=g\left(\frac{R}{R+R}\right)=\frac{g}{2}$ Acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to twice the radius of the earth $g^{\prime \prime}=g\left(\frac{R}{R+2 R}\right)=\frac{g}{3}$
Therefore work done $\mathrm{W}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{2} \mathrm{R}$ The energy required to take this body from the surface of the earth to a height equal to twice the radius of the earth $\mathrm{W}^{\prime}=\mathrm{mg} \mathrm{~m}^{\prime \mathrm{h}}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{3} 2 \mathrm{R}$ or $\mathrm{W}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{2} \mathrm{R} \times 2 \times \frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{~W}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car is moving on circular track banked at an angle of $45^{\circ}$. If the maximum permissible speed of the car to avoid slipping is twice the optimum speed of the car to avoid the wear and tear of the tyres, then the coefficient of static friction between the wheels of the car and the road is
questions.solution:
Maximum speed $V_{\max }=\sqrt{\frac{r g(\mu+\tan \theta)}{1-\mu \tan \theta}}$
and optimum speed $V_{\mathrm{o}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{rg} \tan \theta}$
Given $\theta=45^{\circ}$ and $V_{\max }=2 V_0\sqrt{\frac{\operatorname{rg}(\mu+\tan \theta)}{1-\mu \tan \theta}}=2 \sqrt{\operatorname{rg} \tan \theta}$
Squaring both sides $\frac{(\mu+\tan \theta)}{(1-\mu \tan \theta)}=4 \tan \theta\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mu+\tan 45^{\circ}}{1-\mu \tan 45^{\circ}}=4 \tan 45^{\circ} \Rightarrow \frac{\mu+1}{1-\mu}=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \mu+1=4-4 \mu \Rightarrow 5 \mu=3 \therefore \mu=\frac{3}{5}=0.6
\end{aligned}$

If a horizontal force of 5 N is applied on the block, the kinetic energy of the block in a time of 4 s is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ ),

If the magnetic field is $(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \mathrm{T}$ and the electric field is $(-2 \hat{k}) \mathrm{NC}^{-1}$, then the Lorentz force on the particle is

questions.q: The work done in increasing the diameter of a soap bubble from 2 cm to 4 cm is (Surface tension of soap solution $=3.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$ )

In case of soap bubble work done in increasing area

questions.q:
A steel wire of length 3 m and a copper wire of length 2.2 m are connected end to end. When the combination is stretched by a force, the net elongation is 1.05 mm . If the area of cross-section of each wire is $6 \mathrm{~mm}^2$, then the load applied is
(Young's module of steel and copper are respectively $2 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$ and $1.1 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution:
Young's modulus, $\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{A}} \left\lvert\, \frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}}{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{o}}} \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{l}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{A}}} \mathrm{l}_{\mathrm{o}}\right.\begin{aligned}
& \text { Given } \Delta 1_{\mathrm{s}}+\Delta 1_{\mathrm{c}}=1.05 \mathrm{~mm}=1.05 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m} \\
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{~F}}{\mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{s}}} \frac{\ell_{\mathrm{s}}}{\mathrm{~A}_{\mathrm{s}}}+\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{c}}} \frac{\ell_{\mathrm{c}}}{\mathrm{~A}_{\mathrm{c}}}=1.05 \times 10^{-3} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{~F}\left(\frac{3}{2 \times 10^{11} \times 6 \times 10^{-6}}+\frac{2.2}{1.1 \times 10^{12} \times 0 \times 10^{-6}}\right) \\
& =1.05 \times 10^{-3}
\end{aligned}$
Solving above equation we get load applied $\mathrm{F}=180 \mathrm{~N}$

questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 12 minutes. The time gap between $28 \%$ decay and $82 \%$ decay of the radioactive substance is
questions.solution:
Given half-life $\mathrm{T}_{1 / 2}=12$ minutes.
Time gap between $28 \%$ decay i.e., $100-100 \times \frac{28}{100}=72$ and $82 \%$ decay i.e., $100-100 \times \frac{82}{100}=18$
Therefore $72 \xrightarrow{t_{1 / 2}=12 \mathrm{~min}} 36 \xrightarrow{t_{1 / 2}=12 \mathrm{~min}} 18$
so time gap $=12+12=24$ minutes

questions.q: In a time ' $t$ ', the amplitude of vibrations of a damped oscillator becomes half of its initial value, then the mechanical energy of the oscillator decreases by
questions.solution:
The variation in amplitude of damped harmonic oscillator with time $t$ is given by $A=A_0 e^{-b t}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{A}_0}{2}=\mathrm{A}_0 \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{bt}} \therefore \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{bt}}=\mathbf{2}$
For a damped oscillator if the damping is small then the mechanical energy decreases exponentially as $\mathrm{E}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{kx}^2 \mathrm{e}^{-bt}$

questions.q: For a combination of two convex lenses of focal lengths ' $f_1{ }^{\prime}$ and ' $f_2$ ' to act as a glass slab, the distance of separation between them is
questions.solution:
In case of glass slab $F=\infty$
If equivalent focal length of convex lenses of focal lengths $f_1$ and $f_2$ separated by a distance $d$ (suppose) is infinity then the combination of lenses will act as a glass slab
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{F}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}-\frac{d}{f_1 f_2} \\
& \text { or, } \frac{1}{\infty}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}-\frac{d}{f_1 f_2} \Rightarrow 0=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}-\frac{d}{f_1 f_2} \\
& \text { or, } 0=\frac{f_1+f_2}{f_1+f_2}-\frac{d}{f_1 f_2} \therefore d=f_1+f_2
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The temperatures of equal masses of three different liquids $A, B$ and $C$ are $15^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 24^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ respectively. The resultant temperature when liquids $A$ and $B$ are mixed is $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and when liquids $B$ and $C$ are mixed is $26^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Then the ratio of specific heat capacities of the liquids $A, B$ and $C$ is
questions.solution:
Temperature of mixture of liquids of same mass
$T_{A B}=\frac{T_A C_A+T_B C_B}{C_A+C_B}$
when liquids A and B mixed
$20=\frac{15 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{A}}+24 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{A}}+\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}} \Rightarrow 20 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{A}}+20 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}=15 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{A}}+24 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}$
or, $5 C_A=4 C_B\qquad ...\mathrm{(i)}$
Similarly when liquids B and C are mixed
$26=\frac{24 C_B+30 C_C}{C_B+C_C} \Rightarrow 26 \mathrm{C}_B+26 C_C=24 C_B+30 \mathrm{C}_C$
or, $2 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}=4 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{C}}\therefore \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}=2 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{C}}\qquad ...\mathrm{(ii)}$
From eq. (i) and (ii)
$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{A}}: \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}: \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{C}}=8: 10: 5$

questions.q: Young's double slit experiment is performed with monochromatic light of wavelength 6000 A . If the intensity of light at a point on the screen where path difference of $2000 Å$ is $I_1$ and the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is $1000 Å$ is $I_2$, then $I_1: I_2=$
questions.solution:
Intensity $I=I_0 \cos ^2 \phi$ And $\phi=\frac{2 \pi}{\pi} . \Delta x$ where $\Delta x=$ path difference $\phi_1=\frac{2 \pi}{6000} \times 2000=120^{\circ}$
Similarly, $\phi_2=\frac{2 \pi}{6000} \times 1000=60^{\circ}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{I_1}{I_2}=\frac{I_0 \cos ^2 \phi_1}{I_0 \cos ^2 \phi_2}=\frac{\cos ^2 120^{\circ}}{\cos ^2 60^{\circ}}=\frac{(-1 / 2)}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}=\frac{1}{3} \\ & \therefore I_1: I_2=1: 3 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave in a stretched string ' $A$ ' is ' $v$ '. Another string ' $B$ ' of same length and same radius is subjected to same tension. If the density of the material of the string ' $B$ ' is $2 \%$ more than that of ' $A$ ', then the speed of the transverse wave in string ' $B$ ' is
questions.solution:
Frequency $n=\frac{V}{\lambda}=\sqrt{\frac{T}{\pi r^2 d}}$ where $d=$ density $\therefore \mathrm{V}=\lambda \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\pi \mathrm{r}^2 \mathrm{~d}}} \text { so here } \mathrm{V} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{~d}}}$
If the density of the material of the string B is $2 \%$ more than that of $A$ then $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{V}^{\prime} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{~d}+\mathrm{d} \times \frac{2}{100}}} \text { or } \mathrm{V}^{\prime} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{~d}(1+0.2)}} \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{V}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{V}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{\mathrm{~d}(1.02)}} \left\lvert\, \sqrt{\frac{1}{\mathrm{~d}}} \therefore \mathrm{~V}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\sqrt{1.02}}\right. \end{aligned}$
